candidate_relations.reason: Prominent visual hallucinations, fluctuations, and catatonic signs (echopraxia, mitmachen, mutism) favor Lewy-body rather than typical Alzheimer disease.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Alzheimer vs Lewy-body dementia causing catatonia

candidate_relations.reason: Dementia with Lewy bodies fits the visual hallucinations and inattention but omits the catatonia that is required in the reference object.
Recent mirtazapine may aggravate psychosis, yet three months of decline with echopraxia, mitmachen, and staring indicate DLB-related catatonia rather than isolated drug-induced psychosis.

case_quality_flags: Catatonic signs are well documented, but Lewy body dementia is a clinical inference without dopaminergic imaging or neuropathology.
